DEX_PROGRAM().notice: The one Solana program this router will ever invoke.

_deposit(address,bytes32,uint64,uint64,u.notice: external-for-self so zapIn can reuse the deposit meta assembly with the original user's ATAs. Reverts for any other caller.

pause().notice: Callable by the pauser OR the owner. Idempotent — a 3am double-pause must not revert.

pauser().notice: Single pauser address (rotatable via setPauser; zero disables it). The operator fans its own key out if it wants more than one hot pauser — a set adds storage + enumeration to a non-upgradeable contract for nothing. owner can always pause directly too (see pause()).

pendingOwner().notice: Two-step ownership: proposed next owner, until it accepts. Lets the owner hand control to a multisig/timelock without risking a typo-locked address.

registerPool(bytes32,bytes32[7]).notice: Add-only in place: a live row can never be silently overwritten (AlreadyRegistered). To correct a mis-registration, use unregisterPool() then registerPool() — two owner-gated txs, two events, both blocked once freeze() is called. freeze() permanently locks the REGISTRY; it does NOT stop trading against rows already registered — pause() does that.

route(bytes32,bool,bytes32,bool,uint64,u.notice: Atomic 2-pool route (e.g. USDC→SOL on one tier, SOL→USDC on another — or A→B→C across pairs). The mid amount is read back on-chain, so the second hop swaps exactly what the first yielded. One EVM tx, atomic.

setPauser(address).notice: Rotates the pauser. Zero address disables pauser-initiated pause with no special-cased branch elsewhere — pause() simply never matches it.

unpause().notice: Owner-only (not the pauser) — bounds a compromised pauser key to an owner-undoable DoS, and prevents flapping during an incident.

unregisterPool(bytes32).notice: Removes a row so it can be re-registered with corrected accounts. Pool ids are REUSABLE by design — the id is the on-chain swapState PDA, and a re-registration only re-points the auxiliary accounts stored here; the Solana program validates them against real pool state at CPI time, so a wrong row fails closed, never a silent theft. Available even while frozen is false is required for the incident flow: pause() → this → registerPool() with corrected accounts → verify → unpause().

zapIn(bytes32,bool,uint64,uint64,uint64).notice: Atomic zap-in: swap `amountIn` of the input side, then deposit BOTH sides for LP — one EVM tx, all-or-nothing. The realized swap output AND the pool state are read back on-chain (account_u64_at), so the LP amount is computed from post-swap reserves — no stale off-chain quote can strand the deposit. `minLp` is the slippage floor; `maxOther` bounds the pre-held other-side spend.
